dataset.description: In this dataset an array of raw data will be collected, and the obtained data will be pre-processed by creating a data compendium. As a result, it will be assessed whether some of the survey questions need to be excluded from further data processing. The data will be coded, systemised, and grouped by arranging tables, data interrelations will be searched for, and the data will be statistically analysed by selecting statistically significant factors. The format of the final dataset to be available for public access. To aid in final dataset documentation, throughout the project, we will maintain a log of when, where, and how data were collected, decisions related to methods, coding, and analysis, statistical analyses, software and instruments used, where data and corresponding documentation are stored.

distribution.title:
In the framework of dataset, a survey will be implemented, to identify objective and subjective factors affecting the decision of post-working-age population to stay in the labour market longer or retire and not to work as well as data from Labour Force Survey and EU-SILC survey. To collect the survey data, it is expected to survey the target group in different ways – on-site and remotely- and by using technology such as QuestionPro or another online survey tool.
To perform the survey, it is planned to cooperate with a professional data collecting company. The survey questionnaire is already on preparation stage and questions will be prepared using different criteria which are prepared during theoretical studies of scientific publications. The survey is confidential and obtained survey data in personal interviews will be processed only in anonymized way. Survey questionnaire structure is organized: introduction part with invitation to participate in the survey, information of the survey aim, confidentiality of respondents and that all obtained data will be used only in updated way to prepare recommendations for policy makers on reasonable and possible involvement is economic and social activities of the population group 65+ in all statistical regions and in territories (urban/rural); main part of questions (opened and closed) to reach the survey aim and at the conclusion part will be demographic part – to analyze survey data in different groups: by age groups, by gender, by territory (urban or rural), by statistical region, etc. The respondent sample will be made by using as stratified random sampling method.

dmp.description:
The Data Management Plan (DMP) is prepared in the framework of the project No 5.2.1.1.i.0/2/24/I/CFLA/007 “Internal and External Consolidation of the University of Latvia” of the second round of the “Consolidation and Governance Change Implementation Grants within Investment 5.2.1.i “Research, Development and Consolidation Grants” under Reform 5.2.1. r. “Higher Education and Science Excellence and Governance Reform” of Reform and Investment Strand 5.2. of the Latvian Recovery and Resilience Mechanism Plan “Ensuring Change in the Governace Model of Higher Education Institutions”, postdoctoral research grant project No LU-BA-PG-2024/1-0017 “Silver economy potential in the regions of Latvia and the factors influencing it” (project manager Dr.sc.admin. Lilita Seimuškāne, 1st September 2024 – 31st August 2025).

Summary of the postdoctoral research grant project
Demographic ageing tendencies both in Europe and Latvia will bring changes to the pyramid of population age structure. Transfer to the population structure with an even greater share of older people will be the most significant change. According to the latest forecasts of the European Commission on the impact of demographic changes in Europe, the number of the working-age population that can contribute to the production of value and formation of society’s income is significantly reducing. It is expected that Latvia will face the most rapid decrease of labour force among the states of the euro area. The forecasts show that the number of people at the working age will drop by 42% till 2070. Changes to the labour market caused by digital transformation affect the re-structuring of economic fields, the creation of new employment forms, and the demand for new knowledge and skills. Along with the decreasing labour force and high migration level, the necessity of using the current human resources including within the context of active ageing becomes more topical in Latvia creating conditions for as inclusive employment as possible. Demographic changes affect society in a very wide scope. They affect both the general growth of the national economy and economy, budget, cost structure, competitiveness, and services of each region and local government. The forecasted tendencies ask to search for timely solution options since the demographic changes are to be a huge challenge to capacity of the states’ fiscal and economic policy. One of the solutions offered is the concept of silver economy. Its philosophy is to change society’s attitude towards the process of population ageing and economic adaptation to the increasing number of elderly people.
For dissemination of the research results and technological knowledge transfer, the post-doctoral researcher will develop one scientific publication targeted at the scientific quality that would conform journal indexation of SCOPUS or Web of Science and submit a new project application in the Fundamental and Applied Research Programme of the Latvian Council of Science by developing a specific study direction on the potential of intergenerational cooperation in promoting inclusive employment of the post-working age population in Latvia.
